content:
alex_support: Customer reports Python SDK streaming generator hangs when the first SSE chunk contains a partial token. They say streaming output stops and generator never yields final text.

nina_support: Can you paste the SDK version + minimal repro? Also any raw logs from the app (showing bytes) would help.

alex_support: Customer env: python 3.10, httpx 0.24.3, redwood-python 0.6.1. Repro steps they gave:
1) open stream with client.stream(...) using default SDK helper
2) iterate generator
3) sometimes it yields nothing (hangs) until connection closes

ben_eng: Likely SSE parsing edge-case where the first network chunk ends mid-json token (e.g. "{\"delta\":\"Hel") and parser waits for the event terminator `\n\n`. Need a tiny reproducer.

alex_support: Here's their raw bytes capture (redacted):
```
--- chunk 1 ---
data: {"id":"evt_1","delta":"Hel
--- chunk 2 ---
lo","role":"assistant"}

--- chunk 3 ---
data: {"id":"evt_2","delta":" worl"
```
In that trace, the generator paused after chunk 1 and didn't flush the partial JSON when chunk 2 arrived.

tim_pysdk: That matches bug we fixed last week — parser didn't handle partial JSON boundaries correctly when the first event lacked a trailing empty line or when keepalive frames (204/empty `data:`) are interleaved. Fixed in redwood-python 0.6.2. Workaround: use the lower-level `.stream_raw()` and accumulate bytes yourself or upgrade.

tori_sre: Additional note: some HTTP client versions (httpx/urllib3) split TCP frames differently which makes this flaky. Repro is sensitive to `httpx` version + OS socket buffer. If you can't upgrade, we can add a small shim to the SDK to flush incomplete events after a short idle (100ms) — less ideal but pragmatic.

alex_support: Minimal repro script customer ran (sanitized):
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)
it = c.stream("chat:generate", model="redwood/latest")
for chunk in it:
    print(repr(chunk))
```
They also provided a custom raw loop that shows the SSE frame split.

nina_support: Can you ask customer to try `pip install redwood-python==0.6.2` and confirm? If they can't, collect a tcpdump or `curl --raw` trace.

ci-bot: Deploy note: redwood-python 0.6.2 released to PyPI (chore/stream-sse-fix). See changelog: https://pypi.org/project/redwood-python/0.6.2

ben_eng: For triage: if they reproduce locally, collect these items: 1) Python version, 2) httpx version, 3) minimal script + exact output, 4) raw bytes capture from `scapy`/tcpdump or middleware, 5) SDK logs with DEBUG.

tim_pysdk: Internals: parser now accumulates until a full event delimiter or EOF, and will also try to parse partial JSON when a `data:` line ends with an incomplete brace and the next chunk arrives. This avoids generator deadlock on split tokens.

nina_support: Customer upgraded and reported back: "issue seems fixed — streaming resumed immediately and tokens arrive as expected" :thumbsup:

alex_support: Closing with notes for the ticket: root cause = SSE parser did not handle JSON split across chunk boundary + httpx chunking. Fix in 0.6.2. Repro steps and raw bytes attached to ticket. Marked resolved.

ben_eng: Follow-up: add unit test that simulates chunking at random offsets and a stress test in CI (httpx compatibility matrix), open follow-up GH issue to test against older httpx versions.

tori_sre: Also add a short troubleshooting FAQ blurb for support: "If streaming hangs, ask customer to upgrade SDK and report http client version + raw bytes".
